title: Lineaments around Mahd adh Dhahab from four NASADEM hillshades
data: NASADEM_HGT version 001 by NASA JPL (2020): 1 arc-second (about 30 m) elevations from the SRTM flight of February 2000, in whole metres above the EGM96 geoid, tiles n23e040 and n23e041.
method: Read a 30 × 30 km window (EPSG:32637, x 675015 to 705015, y 2585015 to 2615015) and reprojected it to 30 m cells; elevation runs from 921 to 1,305 m.
Four hillshades lit from 0°, 45°, 90° and 135°, sun 30° high, vertical exaggeration 2.
Canny edge detection (2-pixel smoothing, thresholds at the 80th and 90th percentiles of gradient), then a probabilistic Hough transform: minimum length 600 m, maximum gap 90 m.
Merged the four directions from longest to shortest, dropping a line when more than half of it lies within 60 m of a kept line.
limits: Lineaments are linear terrain features, not confirmed faults: they include ridge edges, wadi floors, road cuts and pits, and structural interpretation stays with the geologist. Cells are 30 m and the minimum length is 600 m, so shorter lines and lines buried under sand on the plains are missed. The NASADEM user guide (NASA JPL, 2020) gives the SRTM requirement as 16 m absolute vertical error at 90% and a global average absolute height error of about 6.8 m.
